whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before It's Too Late

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Firmly Set
items.desc: Most personal injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on compensation.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still recover a portion of damages. We can help clarify how fault might be apportioned in your situation.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic harm. That makes an accurate case evaluation especially important.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand. Fees only come from a successful recovery.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Rolling Hills Estates?
items.answer: Under California law, most injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If your claim involves a government entity, such as a public road issue, the window can be as short as six months, so it's wise to act sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Rolling Hills Estates?
items.answer: Public collision records show that Palos Verdes Drive North, Palos Verdes Drive East, Hawthorne Boulevard, and Silver Spur Road have the highest recorded crash counts in the city, with reports tending to peak on Thursdays around midday. These are neutral public-record patterns, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so being partially responsible doesn't automatically prevent you from recovering compensation. Your potential recovery may simply be reduced by your share of fault, which we can help evaluate.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews. We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.

items.question: Is there a cap on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In most ordinary personal injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering. The specific facts of your case will determine what compensation may be appropriate, which is something we can assess.
